diff_user.system: You are optimizing a Go function. Popcount(xs []uint64) int must return the total number of set bits across all words of xs. Each candidate is scored by running it in giri, a Go SSA interpreter, on 50 test vectors. It must return the reference result on every vector, and leave xs unchanged. Among correct candidates, a lower abstract cost (the number of SSA instructions executed over all vectors) scores higher, and any correct candidate scores above any incorrect one. The only import allowed is math/bits. Keep the function's name and signature.
responses:
The current kernel is already a tuned, fully unrolled ladder with no per-word loop overhead beyond one reslice per 16 words. I don't have a reliable model of giri's per-instruction costs, so I can't predict the gains from micro-changes with confidence. The one change I expect to help is a larger unrolled block for long inputs. It halves the loop-condition and reslice overhead for inputs of 32+ words and leaves the tail ladder untouched. It is a strict superset of the current logic, so correctness is preserved.

Reasoning: for long vectors, the 32-word block replaces two loop iterations with one, saving one length comparison, one branch, and one reslice per 32 words. The 16-word loop and the tail ladder still handle any remainder below 32, so results match the reference for every length. The gain is modest and depends on how giri counts loop overhead versus the 32 popcount calls. If the test vectors are mostly short (under 32 words), the change is roughly neutral, since the extra loop check adds only one comparison per call.
